alex: Morning — ACME reported streaming responses cut out after ~30s and then a 401. They gave request-id r-3a9f2c. Happened twice with same pattern. They say token rotate every 60s. Can we get repro steps and ask for a debug bundle?

maria: Got it. Please paste the ticket and any request ids. Also need exact headers they send (Authorization, x-request-id) and whether they use short-lived tokens or API keys.

alex: Ticket #7892. Logs show: \"auth: token expired\" then \"stream closed by server\". Request IDs: r-3a9f2c, r-3a9f2d. They confirmed client rotates token every 60s. I tried a quick local repro and saw similar disconnect.

alex: Here is the curl I used; it fails consistently after ~25-35s with a 401 in the response headers:

```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Request-Id: r-3a9f2c-local" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"stream test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
```

maria: Please ask them to run that exact curl but with `--trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt` and paste the first 200 lines and the headers. Also have them include `-H \"X-Debug-Client: acct-acme\"` so we can filter logs.

tina_sre: Likely root cause: token rotation while connection is open. Short-lived tokens are fine for request-per-call flows but SSE/HTTP streaming keeps a single connection open; if the client swaps token mid-stream the server's auth layer may reject subsequent frames. Two recommended repro checks:
- Confirm whether client is literally replacing the Authorization header on an open TCP connection (won't change server-side).
- Reproduce by starting stream with an invalid/expired token after ~30s to confirm 401 mid-stream.

tina_sre: Also request server-side audit for r-3a9f2c at auth service: `auth:check` logs and `proxy:conn` logs around the timestamp. If they can share a debug bundle run `redwood collect-debug --request r-3a9f2c --include auth,proxy,streaming` and upload.

alex: I'll ask customer to run both commands. I'll send them a validated curl to run. Also asked them to run with a long-lived API key as a quick workaround.

maria: Share this validated curl for them to copy (replace TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER and XDEBUG):

```bash
TOKEN=REPLACE_ME
curl -v -N --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Request-Id: r-3a9f2c-cust" -H "X-Debug-Client: acct-acme" --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"keep stream open"}' "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate"
```

deploy-bot: [anomaly-detector] brief rise in 401s observed in hosted-eu-1 around 2026-03-12T08:20Z — correlates with token-rotation rollout. Flagged for eng-sre review.

maria: Thanks — once they paste /tmp/trace.txt and the debug bundle link we'll attach to the ticket and escalate to eng-sre if we confirm auth mid-stream failures.

alex: Sending instructions now to customer. Will update when they respond.
